ac.item: Re-running scout:record-check-ins across an hour in which the elected address for a place changes produces exactly one row for that place in that hour
ac.evidence: Proven twice, at unit scale and at seeded scale. (a) Unit: mechanism_1/2/3 tests, each running the command twice with the book mutated between runs, each with a query-layer positive control proving the election actually flipped. (b) Live, 20,000 book rows / 5 geos: run 1 -> 5 rows; run 2 (no change) -> 0 recorded, still 5; run 3 after inserting 5 LOWER address_ids (flipping the winner at every geo) -> 0 recorded, still 5. Positive control: matcher now elects 100-104 while rows still hold frozen 900000-900004. The old key would have produced 10 rows.

ac.item: All three flip mechanisms covered by tests, including the bucket-migration case, which must not strand a stale is_staged
ac.evidence: mechanism_1_a_lower_address_id_opening_at_the_same_geo_does_not_flip_the_winner; mechanism_2_the_winning_orders_closing_does_not_flip_the_winner; mechanism_3_an_address_moving_sides_between_rebuilds_preserves_the_frozen_staged_row_and_adds_a_direct_one. All three mutate clarity.scout_open_addresses between two command runs and carry positive controls. Mechanism 3 is modelled TEMPORALLY (delete the Staging book row, re-insert the same address_id on a Direct hotlist) because production measurement showed 0 of 4,519,947 book address_ids carry both is_staged values, so the simultaneous dual-listing the ticket described cannot occur. Its assertions are sharp enough to fail the real failure mode (two staging rows and no Direct row): total==2 AND exactly one per side AND the staged row's matched_at preserved AND both rows naming address_id 8000.

ac.item: The measured recorded/kits_processed figure from the completed log line is reported before and after
ac.status: NOT SATISFIED — deferred by explicit decision
ac.evidence: Dalton decided 2026-08-25 that the 'after' figure is a POST-MERGE follow-up and does not gate this ticket. Neither figure arrives on its own because routes/console.php:59-65 has the schedule commented out, so both require a manual production run. The PR ships instead: (a) the measured exposure sizing in flip-risk-measurement.md (33.3% of (geo,is_staged) election groups hold >1 address; 59.2% of book rows); (b) a precise procedure in ac3-measurement-procedure.md including the corrected timing rule (start the after-run at least one full lookback_minutes PAST the hour boundary, not merely after the boundary) and the deploy-boundary duplicate that would otherwise inflate it.

ac.item: No regression to DEV-2414's grain: N co-located addresses at one place still yield one row per is_staged side
ac.evidence: several_co_located_addresses_per_side_still_collapse_to_one_row_per_side (3 co-located Direct + 1 co-located Staging -> exactly 2 rows, one per side, correct lowest-address_id winner per side). All 10 pre-existing ScoutCheckInMatchQueryParityTest grain assertions remain green, including test_colocated_direct_and_staging_each_record_their_own_check_in. At seeded scale, 20,000 co-located book rows across 5 geos collapsed to exactly 5 rows.

ac.item: The change must not regress the recorder's production resource footprint (DEV-2342 precedent)
ac.evidence: Marginal peak RSS 3.03 MB over the flag-off control, 0.67s wall clock against a 300s interval, at 20,000 book rows. Allocation is driven by match count (server-side filtering means only elected rows cross the PHP boundary), not book size, so it does not scale with production's larger book. Full figures and controls in .context/qa-resource-envelope.json.

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT <cluster-size bucket>, count(), sum(n) FROM (SELECT count() AS n FROM clarity.scout_open_addresses WHERE geo != 0 GROUP BY tupleElement(geo,1), tupleElement(geo,2), is_staged) GROUP BY bucket
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 2,767,871 (geo,side) groups; 922,021 (33.3%) hold >1 address; 2,674,097 book rows (59.2%) sit in such a group
derivation_log.why: the at-risk population for flip mechanisms 1 and 2 — the figure the ticket says is unmeasured

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT countIf(sides=2), count() FROM (SELECT uniqExact(is_staged) AS sides FROM clarity.scout_open_addresses WHERE geo != 0 GROUP BY address_id)
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 0 of 4,519,947 address_ids carry both is_staged values
derivation_log.why: tests whether mechanism 3's simultaneous dual-listing variant occurs in production — it does not; mechanism 3 must be restated as a temporal label change

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT count(), uniqExact(address_id), uniqExact((hotlist_id,address_id)), uniqExact(hotlist_id) FROM clarity.scout_open_addresses
derivation_log.why: confirms address_id is globally unique in the book snapshot (independent verification of the zero-dual-listing result)

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT countIf(sides=2), count() FROM (SELECT uniqExact(is_staged) AS sides FROM clarity.scout_open_addresses WHERE geo != 0 GROUP BY tupleElement(geo,1), tupleElement(geo,2))
derivation_log.aggregate_result: 404,786 of 2,363,085 geos (17.13%) carry both sides FLEET-WIDE
derivation_log.why: the AC4 both-sides population; distinct from the docblock's ~0.27% per-org view-weighted figure and must not be conflated with it

derivation_log.query_shape: SELECT status, count(), countIf(updated_at >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY), countIf(updated_at >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY) FROM zod.public_hotlist FINAL WHERE _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 GROUP BY status
